approach: Add one field to CheckRun in athena-data: `revert_for: Vec<u32>`, the criterion numbers (from 1) whose planned 'fails without the fix' run this is; empty for every ordinary check (serde default, skipped when empty, like `reused`). This replaces the earlier `revert: bool`, so the marker and its scope are one value that cannot disagree. Athena builds the record from the finished demonstration run with a pure `revert_record(group, run)` in verify.rs: name `fails-without-N`, the plan's command, the run's exit code, tests_ran and output tail, `revert_for = group.criteria`, and `passed = true`. `passed` here means 'not a pass/fail check', so the record never blocks the verdict, as the demonstration view already says. This deviates from the reading's wording, where `passed` meant 'failed as expected'; the change description, the field's doc comment and the changelog say so. In judge(), inside the existing candidate_tree == checks_tree gate, the job-wide `ran` list is left untouched. A second list of revert records that have an exit code is kept instead. While checking criterion number n, a cited piece counts as seen when it is in `ran`, or when a revert record whose `revert_for` contains n has that command or that record name. The rule is therefore enforced per criterion by code. It covers only criteria whose planned demonstration names a fails-without. The code cannot tell which half of one criterion a cited command supports, and the docs say so. `run/checks.rs` returns each run's view and record together, and `verification_stage` appends the records to `check_runs` after the verifier's input view is built, so the brief is unchanged. The carried check lines in reading.rs show a revert record as 'fails-without-1: revert run (exit code 101)'. A small helper in close.rs keeps revert records out of the PR body's 'N checks passed'.

decisions.choice: Mark the record with `revert_for: Vec<u32>` (the criteria it demonstrates) instead of `revert: bool`.
decisions.reason: Finding 2: the 'fails without the fix part only' scope must be enforced, not just written. judge() walks criteria by index (verify.rs 470) and DemonstrationGroup.criteria (verify.rs 706-713) already holds the numbers, so the record carries them. One field is both the marker (non-empty) and the scope, so the two cannot disagree, and no extra record file is needed. An empty value means an ordinary check, as `reused` false does (records.rs 805-809).

rejected.why: Two fields could disagree: a revert flag with no criteria, or criteria on an ordinary check.

rejected.option: Keep `revert: bool` and the job-wide `ran` list, and mark the 'that part only' limit as prose-only
rejected.why: The critic's evidence shows this would count the failing run for the 'passes with the fix' part of any criterion citing the same text. The data to scope it exists, so enforcing it is cheap.
It multiplies records for one run and would repeat the output tail.

decisions.choice: In judge(), keep `ran` as it is, with the existing filter line byte for byte. Build a separate list of revert records, inside the tree-equality gate, only those with an exit code. Test each cited piece against `ran` plus the revert records whose `revert_for` contains the criterion's number (i + 1): their command pieces (via simple_commands of command.join(' ')) and their name.
decisions.reason: This puts the scope in code. A criterion outside the group, a record from another tree, or a run that did not finish gets nothing new. The admission test ci_reuse_replay_the_seen_commands_filter_turns_up_in_a_search_and_must_be_named (admission.rs 1078-1143) searches verify.rs for the filter line, so it stays untouched. The cited name `fails-without-1` is seen only when a revert record of that name exists for that criterion.

rejected.option: Add the revert command and name to the job-wide `ran`
rejected.why: It counts for every behavior criterion, which is the major finding.

rejected.option: Count the record name for any record
rejected.why: A cited name that never ran would be seen, which loosens D43.

decisions.choice: The revert record always has passed = true; its exit code stays as run (for example 101). Say in the doc comment on the field and in the changelog that `passed` is 'not a pass/fail check' for these records, and that this departs from the reading's 'failed as the criterion expected'. Render it in the carried check lines (reading.rs 1880-1895) as '<name>: revert run (exit code N)' instead of 'passed'.
decisions.reason: Existing readers treat `!passed` as a failed check: judge() blocking_checks (verify.rs 384), reading.rs 1933 failed-check carry text, introspect.rs 939-949 and is_pre_existing. A failing revert run is the expected result, so it must not fail the verdict. The demonstration view already states 'no pass or fail of its own' (verify.rs 959-961). The carried-line change stops the next round from reading 'passed (exit code 101)' (finding 3).

rejected.why: A revert run that wrongly passes would then block the verdict and appear as a 'failed check', breaking 64cb889's 'fails nothing' rule.
It is misleading in verification.json and in the next round's brief.

rejected.option: Skip revert records in the carried lines
rejected.why: The next round loses the evidence that the revert run happened. The lines are short and bounded by CARRIED_CHECK_LINES.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests, each with commands_verified false, met forced false and a Major 'cited but not seen running: `...`' finding. Cases: (a) a command nobody ran or recorded; (b) a revert record whose exit_code is None, cited by name and by command; (c) a revert record with the right command and name but checks_tree 'def' (and a case with None) while candidate_tree is 'abc'; (d) a name no record carries; (e) the new out-of-group case: the revert record's revert_for is [3] and the criterion under test (number 2) cites that record's command and name, which stay unseen; (f) the same record cited by criterion 3 is seen.

Cases (a) to (d) already hold on today's code; they are regression guards that fail only if the new rule drops its exit-code or tree gate. Case (e) is the one negative case the new rule can break: it fails if the rule is job-wide.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff of the two docs. CHANGELOG.md `## [Unreleased]` gets a Fixed entry naming the root cause (the revert run was shown but not recorded, so D43 never saw it), the fix, the `passed` meaning and that scope is per criterion. docs/design/job-planning.md gets a paragraph after the 'fails without the fix' text (lines 332-341) stating in prose that the recorded run counts as seen running, by command or record name, only for the criteria whose planned demonstration names that run, never for other criteria and never for a run that did not finish or is from another tree. The paragraph also says plainly that within one such criterion the code cannot tell the 'fails without' half from the 'passes with' half, so that split remains a verifier-judged matter.
demonstrations.observes: The Unreleased entry exists and the design paragraph states the scope, matching what the tests in criterion 3 enforce.

demonstrations.method: The outcome is the test of criterion 1 plus criterion 2: a revert record fails-without-1 with exit 101 cited by command and by name by a criterion in its group gives commands_verified true. Criterion 4's run-level test shows production writes that same shape.
demonstrations.observes: commands_verified true and no D43 finding for that shape. Before the change the same input was unmet with commands_verified false.

open_questions: User: Within one criterion that names a fails-without demonstration, the code cannot tell whether a cited command supports the 'fails without the fix' part or the 'passes with the fix' part, because the reading has no fails_without field (out of scope). The plan scopes the count to the criteria in the group. Is criterion-level scope enough, or should adding that field be a follow-up job?
